resources.title: The Perverted Love Of St Valentine's Day
resources.original_resource_body:
We live in a world where those who suppress the truth have the loudest voices. They are more persuasive in their arguments because their arguments sound logical and well-reasoned. However, the fact that an argument is loud and logical does not necessarily mean it is the truth. At the same time, the fact that an argument is loud and logical does not mean it is of God. So many claim they do not care where it originates from, but they agree with and have bought into its message. If that is your stance, then you need to hear this because what you believe and have bought into is a lie. Remember, ignorance is not bliss but a dangerous position to occupy as many ‘ignorants’ abound in hell!
       The argument for celebrating St. Valentine's Day is loud and sounds logical but it is not the truth, nor is it of God! It is not of God because the love that Jesus Christ portrays carries within it the responsibility of self-sacrifice whilst that of Valentine carries no responsibility but the gratification of self! The celebration has become an avenue for spiritual and commercial exploitation. 
       According to God’s word, the proponents of this evil and its likes know the truth but chose not to obey or walk in the truth: “…Since what can be known about God is evident among them, because God has shown it to them. From the creation of the world His invisible attributes that is, His eternal power and divine nature have been clearly seen, being understood through what He has made. As a result, people are without excuse. For though they knew God, they did not glorify Him as God or show gratitude. Instead, their thinking became nonsense, and their senseless minds were darkened. Claiming to be wise, they became fools and exchanged the glory of the immortal God for images resembling mortal man, birds, four-footed animals and reptiles” (Romans 1:19-23). So as not to fall into such error, God warned us to test all spirits to determine if they are from God because many false prophets moved by false spirits abound in the world.
       The very nature of God is being counterfeited daily and the sons of the Kingdom are buying into these heresies. The Bible tells us that God is love and He revealed His love for us by sending “His One and Only Son into the world so that we might live through Him” (1John 4:9b). Friends, what proof do we have that St Valentine’s ‘love’ is of God? What selfless sacrificial act did the Priest Valentine perform for mankind that was not his duty? Is it in the pairing of young unmarried people with patron saints for a year in the medieval ages by the Church? Obviously, that didn’t work out because the devil’s intention was not complete. Or is it because it claims to celebrate ‘love’?  
       Presently, the ‘love’ of Valentine emphasises both the courtly and erotic love. It is now used as a season to celebrate love between couples, intended couples and those being lusted after! Now, here’s the contradiction: How can a love that emphasises both the courtly and erotic love be pure and be said to come from God? How do we reckon that such a ‘love’ is sufficient to make the human being be more responsive to God and to each other? This ‘love’ is a contradiction in itself! It carries within it the following attributes in its composition: It is illicit, immoral, passionately irresponsible, humiliating and fleshly! All these cannot point one to the true knowledge of God’s love no matter how one spins or tweaks it! You might argue that it has a few good ingredients within it, but how can it be good when the end game is to gratify flesh and not glorify God? 
       Beloved, do you not know that “A little yeast leavens the whole lump of dough” (Galatians 5:9). For instance, a dash of iodine in pure drinking water; the water is impure and unfit for drinking. Thus, an argument that one should concentrate on the good parts of the celebration of love will not make such love pure and godly! The love of God carries within it responsibility. The perverted love of Valentine carries within it zero responsibility: It seeks only to celebrate the object of the ‘love’. No wonder some corporate organisations and groups in the guise of improving teamwork through bonding encourage their employees and members to have secret valentines (objects of their lust). Thus, giving the people an excuse to give and receive amorous advances from someone they are not engaged to or married to. This effectively takes out the personal responsibilities towards each other. 
        When the feelings of responsibility are thrown out of the window, the ground is made ready for illicit, immoral, selfish and humiliating amorous experiences. Even the suggestive gifts given, though look harmless are actually disguised cupid arrows (which is the symbol of Valentine’s perverted love) shot at the hearts of the recipients: “But each person is tempted when he is drawn away and enticed by his own evil desires. Then after desire has conceived, it gives birth to sin, and when sin is fully grown, it gives birth to death” (James 1:15).
       The sad part of these celebrations is the fact that undiscerning Churches organize seminars for the married and singles so that they would not be supposedly carried away by the winds of darkness at this time. Unfortunately, these programs since they were not authorised by God are hijacked by the enemy. In most of these gatherings, brothers have condoms in their pockets just waiting for the fun to begin. Pray tell, why do you think true love which is the very nature of God can be taught only on a day that the enemy has set out to celebrate his perverted love? If true love had been taught every day in that congregation in the past year, there would not be a need to hurriedly put up a program that would seek to checkmate the winds of darkness. The program in itself is a testimony that true love had not been taught in that congregation. If it had, the congregants would know and understand that they do not have to wait until a particular day to show their love to their spouses and that true and pure love truly comes with responsibilities as exemplified by our Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ! 
       You may declare that you do not believe in it but you need to buy presents and show your spouse that you love them. Friend, I must break this to you: You do believe in it and have bought into the idolatry! If not, you will not wait till this day to prove your undying love for your spouse or your fiancé! The fact that Christians are the major culprits in this idolatry goes to show what most pulpits are teaching their congregations: “You yourselves are our testimonial, written in our hearts and yet open for anyone to inspect and read. You are an open letter about Christ which we ourselves have written, not with pen and ink but with the Spirit of the living God. Our message has been engraved not in stone, but in living men and women” (2 Corinthians 3:2-3, J. B. Phillips).

Dear child of God, the ‘love’ of St. Valentine is not of God but from the pit of hell to derail and corrupt as many as will buy into its wares! 
God bless you!

We live in a world where those who suppress the truth have the loudest voices. They are more persuasive in their arguments because their arguments sound logical and well-reasoned. However, the fact that an argument is loud and logical does not necessarily mean it is the truth. At the same time, the fact that an argument is loud and logical does not mean it is of God. So many claim they do not care where it originates from, but they agree with and have bought into its message. If that is your stance, then you need to hear this because what you believe and have bought into is a lie. Remember, ignorance is not bliss but a dangerous position to occupy as many ‘ignorants’ abound in hell!

The argument for celebrating St. Valentine's Day is loud and sounds logical but it is not the truth, nor is it of God! It is not of God because the love that Jesus Christ portrays carries within it the responsibility of self-sacrifice whilst that of Valentine carries no responsibility but the gratification of self! The celebration has become an avenue for spiritual and commercial exploitation.

According to God’s word, the proponents of this evil and its likes know the truth but chose not to obey or walk in the truth: “…Since what can be known about God is evident among them, because God has shown it to them. From the creation of the world His invisible attributes that is, His eternal power and divine nature have been clearly seen, being understood through what He has made. As a result, people are without excuse. For though they knew God, they did not glorify Him as God or show gratitude. Instead, their thinking became nonsense, and their senseless minds were darkened. Claiming to be wise, they became fools and exchanged the glory of the immortal God for images resembling mortal man, birds, four-footed animals and reptiles” (Romans 1:19-23). So as not to fall into such error, God warned us to test all spirits to determine if they are from God because many false prophets moved by false spirits abound in the world.

The very nature of God is being counterfeited daily and the sons of the Kingdom are buying into these heresies. The Bible tells us that God is love and He revealed His love for us by sending “His One and Only Son into the world so that we might live through Him” (1John 4:9b). Friends, what proof do we have that St Valentine’s ‘love’ is of God? What selfless sacrificial act did the Priest Valentine perform for mankind that was not his duty? Is it in the pairing of young unmarried people with patron saints for a year in the medieval ages by the Church? Obviously, that didn’t work out because the devil’s intention was not complete. Or is it because it claims to celebrate ‘love’?

Presently, the ‘love’ of Valentine emphasises both the courtly and erotic love. It is now used as a season to celebrate love between couples, intended couples and those being lusted after! Now, here’s the contradiction: How can a love that emphasises both the courtly and erotic love be pure and be said to come from God? How do we reckon that such a ‘love’ is sufficient to make the human being be more responsive to God and to each other? This ‘love’ is a contradiction in itself! It carries within it the following attributes in its composition: It is illicit, immoral, passionately irresponsible, humiliating and fleshly! All these cannot point one to the true knowledge of God’s love no matter how one spins or tweaks it! You might argue that it has a few good ingredients within it, but how can it be good when the end game is to gratify flesh and not glorify God?

Beloved, do you not know that “A little yeast leavens the whole lump of dough” (Galatians 5:9). For instance, a dash of iodine in pure drinking water; the water is impure and unfit for drinking. Thus, an argument that one should concentrate on the good parts of the celebration of love will not make such love pure and godly! The love of God carries within it responsibility. The perverted love of Valentine carries within it zero responsibility: It seeks only to celebrate the object of the ‘love’. No wonder some corporate organisations and groups in the guise of improving teamwork through bonding encourage their employees and members to have secret valentines (objects of their lust). Thus, giving the people an excuse to give and receive amorous advances from someone they are not engaged to or married to. This effectively takes out the personal responsibilities towards each other.

When the feelings of responsibility are thrown out of the window, the ground is made ready for illicit, immoral, selfish and humiliating amorous experiences. Even the suggestive gifts given, though look harmless are actually disguised cupid arrows (which is the symbol of Valentine’s perverted love) shot at the hearts of the recipients: “But each person is tempted when he is drawn away and enticed by his own evil desires. Then after desire has conceived, it gives birth to sin, and when sin is fully grown, it gives birth to death” (James 1:15).

The sad part of these celebrations is the fact that undiscerning Churches organize seminars for the married and singles so that they would not be supposedly carried away by the winds of darkness at this time. Unfortunately, these programs since they were not authorised by God are hijacked by the enemy. In most of these gatherings, brothers have condoms in their pockets just waiting for the fun to begin. Pray tell, why do you think true love which is the very nature of God can be taught only on a day that the enemy has set out to celebrate his perverted love? If true love had been taught every day in that congregation in the past year, there would not be a need to hurriedly put up a program that would seek to checkmate the winds of darkness. The program in itself is a testimony that true love had not been taught in that congregation. If it had, the congregants would know and understand that they do not have to wait until a particular day to show their love to their spouses and that true and pure love truly comes with responsibilities as exemplified by our Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ!

You may declare that you do not believe in it but you need to buy presents and show your spouse that you love them. Friend, I must break this to you: You do believe in it and have bought into the idolatry! If not, you will not wait till this day to prove your undying love for your spouse or your fiancé! The fact that Christians are the major culprits in this idolatry goes to show what most pulpits are teaching their congregations: “You yourselves are our testimonial, written in our hearts and yet open for anyone to inspect and read. You are an open letter about Christ which we ourselves have written, not with pen and ink but with the Spirit of the living God. Our message has been engraved not in stone, but in living men and women” (2 Corinthians 3:2-3, J. B. Phillips).

Dear child of God, the ‘love’ of St. Valentine is not of God but from the pit of hell to derail and corrupt as many as will buy into its wares!

God bless you!

resources.title: Before You Speak...
resources.original_resource_body:
"Death and life are in the power of the tongue, And those who love it will eat its fruit" (Proverbs 18:21). 
       Have you noticed that one of the things the enemy has succeeded in doing is changing definitions of certain words? Such that words that were plainly understood now have double meanings. And of course, neither of the meanings is exactly what the meaning of the word should be. Some words, allow your imagination to run while actually meaning something different. The whole idea is not just to demystify language but to demystify the power of words on our tongue. 
       Now, when you think words don't matter, or they matter in certain circumstances and not in others, you will speak without guardrails on your tongue. What this means is you will mean one thing in certain circumstances and something else in another circumstance. Hence the words "I really didn't mean it like that"! Sadly, the damage will be done. 
       Beloved, words are powerful. More so as children of God. We do not see God mincing or wasting His Word. What He says He means and it stands. If we claim to be His children, then we must understand that our words matter too no matter the circumstances we find ourselves. 
       To underscore this truth, let's consider Jacob and Rachel! In Genesis 31, when Laban pursued Jacob over the stolen idols, Jacob responded with confidence and anger: "If you find your gods with anyone here, he will not live!...Jacob did not know that Rachel had stolen the idols" (Genesis 31: 32). Those were not just mere words. It was a Sentence! What made this moment sad is that Jacob did not know that it was Rachel—the woman he loved deeply, the woman he laboured 14 years for—who had taken those idols. But God heard him. And that’s the danger!
       We speak in ignorance, but forget that our words still carry weight and resound in Heaven. Not long after, in Genesis 35:16-20, Rachel dies while giving birth to Benjamin. You may argue it is coincidence. Maybe. But spiritually, it teaches something deeper: Words are not empty! 
       The Bible tells us "Death and life are in the power of the tongue, And those who love it will eat its fruit" (Proverbs 18:21). Beloved, not just life… not just death… both. The LORD equally said "Say to them, ‘As I live,’ says the Lord, ‘just as you have spoken in My hearing, so I will do to you..." (Numbers 14:28). Jacob loved Rachel, but in a moment of anger and pressure, he spoke carelessly forgetting that the love of his life was very capable of what her father was accusing! 
       And this is where many of us miss it. We don’t curse our enemies but we curse the people we claim to love—unknowingly. In anger, we say things we don’t mean, in frustration, we speak words we can’t take back, in ignorance, we release what we don’t understand. And later (sadly), we wonder why things begin to die—relationships, peace, joy, even destinies. 
       Beloved, lives are built, sustained and torn down by the words of our mouth without us realising! Don't be deceived, words are spiritual seeds. Once released, they don’t return empty, they deliver on what they were crafted and sent out to do. You can love someone deeply and still damage them with your mouth. Jacob is proof of that! This is why it is wisdom to know what to say and when to be silent. Especially in these difficult and trying times! 
      We must ask the LORD for wisdom in knowing that not every situation requires a reaction. Not every accusation requires a declaration, rebuttal or defence. Most times, Silence is Protection! These are the times we must learn vigilance, not just about our surroundings and the person(s) we perceive as enemies, but things we say, passionately or dispassionately. resources.normalized_resource_body:
"Death and life are in the power of the tongue, And those who love it will eat its fruit" (Proverbs 18:21).

Have you noticed that one of the things the enemy has succeeded in doing is changing definitions of certain words? Such that words that were plainly understood now have double meanings. And of course, neither of the meanings is exactly what the meaning of the word should be. Some words, allow your imagination to run while actually meaning something different. The whole idea is not just to demystify language but to demystify the power of words on our tongue.

Now, when you think words don't matter, or they matter in certain circumstances and not in others, you will speak without guardrails on your tongue. What this means is you will mean one thing in certain circumstances and something else in another circumstance. Hence the words "I really didn't mean it like that"! Sadly, the damage will be done.

Beloved, words are powerful. More so as children of God. We do not see God mincing or wasting His Word. What He says He means and it stands. If we claim to be His children, then we must understand that our words matter too no matter the circumstances we find ourselves.

To underscore this truth, let's consider Jacob and Rachel! In Genesis 31, when Laban pursued Jacob over the stolen idols, Jacob responded with confidence and anger: "If you find your gods with anyone here, he will not live!...Jacob did not know that Rachel had stolen the idols" (Genesis 31: 32). Those were not just mere words. It was a Sentence! What made this moment sad is that Jacob did not know that it was Rachel—the woman he loved deeply, the woman he laboured 14 years for—who had taken those idols. But God heard him. And that’s the danger!

We speak in ignorance, but forget that our words still carry weight and resound in Heaven. Not long after, in Genesis 35:16-20, Rachel dies while giving birth to Benjamin. You may argue it is coincidence. Maybe. But spiritually, it teaches something deeper: Words are not empty!

The Bible tells us "Death and life are in the power of the tongue, And those who love it will eat its fruit" (Proverbs 18:21). Beloved, not just life… not just death… both. The LORD equally said "Say to them, ‘As I live,’ says the Lord, ‘just as you have spoken in My hearing, so I will do to you..." (Numbers 14:28). Jacob loved Rachel, but in a moment of anger and pressure, he spoke carelessly forgetting that the love of his life was very capable of what her father was accusing!

And this is where many of us miss it. We don’t curse our enemies but we curse the people we claim to love—unknowingly. In anger, we say things we don’t mean, in frustration, we speak words we can’t take back, in ignorance, we release what we don’t understand. And later (sadly), we wonder why things begin to die—relationships, peace, joy, even destinies.

Beloved, lives are built, sustained and torn down by the words of our mouth without us realising! Don't be deceived, words are spiritual seeds. Once released, they don’t return empty, they deliver on what they were crafted and sent out to do. You can love someone deeply and still damage them with your mouth. Jacob is proof of that! This is why it is wisdom to know what to say and when to be silent. Especially in these difficult and trying times!

We must ask the LORD for wisdom in knowing that not every situation requires a reaction. Not every accusation requires a declaration, rebuttal or defence. Most times, Silence is Protection! These are the times we must learn vigilance, not just about our surroundings and the person(s) we perceive as enemies, but things we say, passionately or dispassionately. The recipients may deserve it. But the consequences may be hard even for us to bear.

Hence, if I may say, under God, be careful of statements like: “I’m done with you.” “You will never succeed.” “Nothing good will come out of this.” They may feel and sound like harmless expressions spoken out of justifiable anger or a moment of hurt… but they have the power to carry lasting consequences. Also, understand this, life has a way of responding to what is consistently spoken. God had promised this in Numbers 14:28 and Psalm 2:8. Instead, "Your speech should always be gracious, seasoned with salt, so that you may know how you should answer each person" (Colossians 4:6).

Therefore, speak life, even when you are hurt; speak wisdom, even when you are angry; speak blessings even when you don’t fully understand the situation. Because one careless word, sentence, one emotional reaction, one moment without control can open doors you never intended to open! Remember, Jacob loved Rachel, but his words worked against his love.

Finally, let this be a reminder: Before you speak, ask yourself—“Am I building… or am I destroying?” "Is this what the LORD would want me to say at this time?" Because sometimes, the greatest battles we face are not necessarily outside…They are right on our lips. Also, before you go accusing someone else of failing in this, why not take a mirror and check yourself first? God bless you as we look at the Perfect Word of God in this matter and make amends where necessary.

resources.title: Time To Search For And Hold Fast To GOD'S WORD
resources.original_resource_body:
"And He [that same Jesus Himself] is the propitiation (the atoning sacrifice) for our sins, and not for ours alone but also for [the sins of] the whole world" (1John 2:2, AMPC).
       Jesus Christ came to the world, lived (to show man how to live) and died as a Sacrifice for the sin of mankind; and He is coming back again for us to be with Him forever. For as many as believe in Him and appropriate His sacrifice to their lives, they are saved. Saved from the wrath of the Almighty God to come on the sin of the world! God hates the sin, but He loves His creation. Hence He came in the flesh and took the condemnation and the eternal punishment of sin from mankind upon Himself. This is a sacrifice no other god or name has ever contemplated or done for their adherents throughout the centuries, since the creation of the Universe! Now, here is the crux of the matter. 
       You may have believed Him; it is good, but it is not enough! The Bible tells us there is one more step you must take: "So Jesus said to those Jews who had believed in Him, If you abide in My word [hold fast to My teachings and live in accordance with them], you are truly My disciples" (John 8:31, AMPC). Why must they 'hold fast' to His teachings? Because the devil, the enemy of the soul of man, just as he did in the Garden in the beginning, will try to steal the Word (teachings) from their hearts by misrepresenting the Word. But as they hold fast and continue in the teachings, and live in accordance with what they have learnt, it would be nearly impossible for the devil to steal the Word from their hearts. Jesus Christ called them His Disciples! 
       The Bible went on to describe these ones as righteous. Meaning, they do what is right by deliberately living a life that is pleasing to the LORD, in their actions and word: "No one born (begotten) of God [deliberately, knowingly, and habitually] practices sin, for God's nature abides in him [His principle of life, the divine sperm, remains permanently within him]; and he cannot practice sinning because he is born (begotten) of God" (1John 3:9, AMPC). 
       Thus, a demarcation is drawn between those that are true Disciples of Jesus Christ and those that pay lip service to Him: "By this it is made clear who take their nature from God and are His children and who take their nature from the devil and are his children: no one who does not practice righteousness [who does not conform to God's will in purpose, thought, and action] is of God; neither is anyone who does not love his brother (his fellow believer in Christ)" (1John 3:10, AMPC). Because the devil knows his time is short, he has entered the Church and recruited among those who think they can live unrighteously and still claim the name of the LORD! These ones, at the drop of a hat, deny the deity of Jesus Christ. They realise that the Word of God does not condone their lifestyles and make a lie of their professed belief in the LORD Jesus. 
        This is not random but a coordinated attack on the Church of the Living God from the pit of hell. The reason why so many within the Church are denying the Lordship of Christ over their lives is that they were never part of Him from the onset: "They went out from us, but they did not belong to us; for if they had belonged to us, they would have remained with us. However, they went out so that it might be made clear that none of them belongs to us" (1John 2:19). Yes, they believed Him, but they did not continue (hold fast) in the Word they had heard. Hence, the enemy was able to sow doubt about the Word they had heard in their hearts. Like the Woman in the Garden, they had been promised independence and self-worth if they were able to question and deny the deity of He Who had come to live and die for their sin. 
       Beloved, the Return of the LORD Jesus Christ is imminent. The devil knows his time is short and has stepped up his wrath upon the world. The days of dilly-dallying with the Word of God have passed. This is the time to read, study and put in practice earnestly what you have learned. Do not be like the five Foolish Virgins who thought there was still time and were sure the Wise ones would do the "Christian thing" and share their oil with them. 
       Beloved, look again in the mirror and make sure what is reflected makes true this Scripture in your life: "Beloved, we are [even here and] now God's children; it is not yet disclosed (made clear) what we shall be [hereafter], but we know that when He comes and is manifested, we shall [as God's children] resemble and be like Him, for we shall see Him just as He [really] is" (1John 3:2, AMPC). And NOT: "Why do you misunderstand what I say? It is because you are unable to hear what I am saying. [You cannot bear to listen to My message; your ears are shut to My teaching.] You are of your father, the devil, and it is your will to practice the lusts and gratify the desires [which are characteristic] of your father. He was a murderer from the beginning and does not stand in the truth, because there is no truth in him. When he speaks a falsehood, he speaks what is natural to him, for he is a liar [himself] and the father of lies and of all that is false" (John 8:43-44, AMPC). 
       May the LORD Grant you the grace to sincerely see yourself in the mirror of God’s Word and make the adjustments where necessary, in Jesus Christ Name, Amen! God bless you.

resources.normalized_resource_body:
"And He [that same Jesus Himself] is the propitiation (the atoning sacrifice) for our sins, and not for ours alone but also for [the sins of] the whole world" (1John 2:2, AMPC).

Jesus Christ came to the world, lived (to show man how to live) and died as a Sacrifice for the sin of mankind; and He is coming back again for us to be with Him forever. For as many as believe in Him and appropriate His sacrifice to their lives, they are saved. Saved from the wrath of the Almighty God to come on the sin of the world! God hates the sin, but He loves His creation. Hence He came in the flesh and took the condemnation and the eternal punishment of sin from mankind upon Himself. This is a sacrifice no other god or name has ever contemplated or done for their adherents throughout the centuries, since the creation of the Universe! Now, here is the crux of the matter.

You may have believed Him; it is good, but it is not enough! The Bible tells us there is one more step you must take: "So Jesus said to those Jews who had believed in Him, If you abide in My word [hold fast to My teachings and live in accordance with them], you are truly My disciples" (John 8:31, AMPC). Why must they 'hold fast' to His teachings? Because the devil, the enemy of the soul of man, just as he did in the Garden in the beginning, will try to steal the Word (teachings) from their hearts by misrepresenting the Word. But as they hold fast and continue in the teachings, and live in accordance with what they have learnt, it would be nearly impossible for the devil to steal the Word from their hearts. Jesus Christ called them His Disciples!

The Bible went on to describe these ones as righteous. Meaning, they do what is right by deliberately living a life that is pleasing to the LORD, in their actions and word: "No one born (begotten) of God [deliberately, knowingly, and habitually] practices sin, for God's nature abides in him [His principle of life, the divine sperm, remains permanently within him]; and he cannot practice sinning because he is born (begotten) of God" (1John 3:9, AMPC).

Thus, a demarcation is drawn between those that are true Disciples of Jesus Christ and those that pay lip service to Him: "By this it is made clear who take their nature from God and are His children and who take their nature from the devil and are his children: no one who does not practice righteousness [who does not conform to God's will in purpose, thought, and action] is of God; neither is anyone who does not love his brother (his fellow believer in Christ)" (1John 3:10, AMPC). Because the devil knows his time is short, he has entered the Church and recruited among those who think they can live unrighteously and still claim the name of the LORD! These ones, at the drop of a hat, deny the deity of Jesus Christ. They realise that the Word of God does not condone their lifestyles and make a lie of their professed belief in the LORD Jesus.

This is not random but a coordinated attack on the Church of the Living God from the pit of hell. The reason why so many within the Church are denying the Lordship of Christ over their lives is that they were never part of Him from the onset: "They went out from us, but they did not belong to us; for if they had belonged to us, they would have remained with us. However, they went out so that it might be made clear that none of them belongs to us" (1John 2:19). Yes, they believed Him, but they did not continue (hold fast) in the Word they had heard. Hence, the enemy was able to sow doubt about the Word they had heard in their hearts. Like the Woman in the Garden, they had been promised independence and self-worth if they were able to question and deny the deity of He Who had come to live and die for their sin.

Beloved, the Return of the LORD Jesus Christ is imminent. The devil knows his time is short and has stepped up his wrath upon the world. The days of dilly-dallying with the Word of God have passed. This is the time to read, study and put in practice earnestly what you have learned. Do not be like the five Foolish Virgins who thought there was still time and were sure the Wise ones would do the "Christian thing" and share their oil with them.

Beloved, look again in the mirror and make sure what is reflected makes true this Scripture in your life: "Beloved, we are [even here and] now God's children; it is not yet disclosed (made clear) what we shall be [hereafter], but we know that when He comes and is manifested, we shall [as God's children] resemble and be like Him, for we shall see Him just as He [really] is" (1John 3:2, AMPC). And NOT: "Why do you misunderstand what I say? It is because you are unable to hear what I am saying. [You cannot bear to listen to My message; your ears are shut to My teaching.] You are of your father, the devil, and it is your will to practice the lusts and gratify the desires [which are characteristic] of your father. He was a murderer from the beginning and does not stand in the truth, because there is no truth in him. When he speaks a falsehood, he speaks what is natural to him, for he is a liar [himself] and the father of lies and of all that is false" (John 8:43-44, AMPC).

May the LORD Grant you the grace to sincerely see yourself in the mirror of God’s Word and make the adjustments where necessary, in Jesus Christ Name, Amen! God bless you.

resources.title: Living In The Presence of God
resources.original_resource_body:
“You will show me the path of life; In Your presence is fullness of joy; At Your right hand are pleasures forevermore” (Psalm 16:11).
       A brother was teaching in a Bible Study that a man who has Christ has everything. In the same breath, he added that to make a mark in this generation, one must have money and influence. He concluded that who you know matters, as it opens doors to wealth for as many as are diligent. To this brother, standing in the Presence of reputable and influential men will open doors of wealth to his congregants. Sadly, this is the dilemma of many within the Body of Christ: the desire to eat from the table of God and, at the same time, feed from the table of the world (1 Corinthians 10:21-22). 
       The statement of the brother sounds true but is able to lead a man away from the LORD Jesus Christ. He started well but veered off because of the lust for the things of the world. Yes, we do need the things the world provides, but the principles behind them, if allowed to capture our hearts, have the power to steal our hearts from God. The belief that we need these things side by side with our need for God has made many to believe Jesus Christ with their lips, but their hearts are far from Him. They pay lip service to: "But seek (aim at and strive after) first of all His kingdom and His righteousness (His way of doing and being right), and then all these things taken together will be given you besides"(Matthew 6:33, AMPC). 
       The need for the necessities that will make life easier has made many to love the things of the world more than they love God. This is an age-old problem and a dangerous one: to think one can eat from the table of God and balance it with the table of the world: "Or do we want to make the Lord jealous? Do we think that we are stronger than He"(1Corinthians 10:22, GNT)? The Bible tells us: "You used to live in sin, just like the rest of the world, obeying the devil—the commander of the powers in the unseen world. He is the spirit at work in the hearts of those who refuse to obey God" (Ephesians 2:2, NLT). If we have renounced the world, its systems, and its way of doing things, we no longer live under the influence of the Presence of the devil but now live in the PRESENCE OF GOD.
       Sadly, many within the Body still struggle with this. No wonder the Psalmist asked: "How can a young man keep his way pure..." (Psalm 119: 9a)? This question is important, and how we answer determines whose Presence we live in and whose Table we feed from. And we were told: "By keeping Your word, I have sought You with all my heart; don't let me wander from Your commands. I have treasured Your word in my heart so that I may not sin against You" (Psalm 119: 9b-11). Jesus went further to show us how important God's word is to our living. He told the devil: "...It is written, Man shall not live and be sustained by (on) bread alone but by every word and expression of God" (Luke 4:4, AMPC). 
       The things of the world and from the table of the world may look good, but they cannot sustain man. In fact, they are designed to dull the senses of man and lead him completely away from God (Daniel 1). Beloved, when God created the trees and all vegetation, He spoke to the ground to bring forth vegetation and fruit-bearing trees. When He was going to create the living creatures and fishes in the seas, He spoke to the waters to bring forth the living creatures. When He was going to create man, He spoke to Himself. This is why when you remove the vegetation and all trees from the land, they die. If you remove the fishes and all sea creatures from their habitat, they die. Humans know this! Why then is it difficult for man to understand that without God he cannot live? 
       We see this play out with Moses in the wilderness. When the LORD told Moses that His Presence would no longer go with the children of Israel because of their sin, Moses knew that was like taking a fish out of its habitat. It becomes fair game to every predator. Moses pleaded with the LORD not to send them on the journey without His Presence. He understood the power in living and operating in the Presence of God. The Presence of God is the natural habitat of man. In Him we have everything: "for in Him we live and move and have our being, as also some of your own poets have said, ‘For we are also His offspring’ ” (Acts 17:28). In Him is the foundation of everything. In fact, in His Presence all things consist. Hence the saying that He that has the LORD Jesus Christ has everything. 
       You may seek His blessing, provision, mercy, grace, etc. It is the Presence of God that makes everything worthwhile. It is His Presence that distinguishes us from others: "And Moses said to the Lord, If Your Presence does not go with us, do not carry us up from here! For by what shall it be known that I and Your people have found favor in Your sight? Is it not in Your going with us so that we are distinguished, I and Your people, from all the other people upon the face of the earth” (Exodus 33:15-16, AMPC)? Psalm 91 is all about a man who dwells in the Presence of God. 
       Beloved, if there is one thing we must ask of the LORD, it is His Presence. Everything you seek is found in His Presence. Outside of His Presence is strife, madness and a theatre of self, as we saw with the life of King Saul! Like Moses, we must hold on to the LORD and declare that "...If Your Presence does not go with us, do not bring us up from here"! The distinction you desire cannot be found anywhere else but in His Presence. Remember to seek Him first; all that you desire, according to His will, will be added to you. 

May the LORD grant us the grace to remain rooted in His Presence, in Jesus Christ name, Amen. God bless you!

He concluded that who you know matters, as it opens doors to wealth for as many as are diligent. To this brother, standing in the Presence of reputable and influential men will open doors of wealth to his congregants. Sadly, this is the dilemma of many within the Body of Christ: the desire to eat from the table of God and, at the same time, feed from the table of the world (1 Corinthians 10:21-22). "},{"type":"hardBreak"},{"type":"text","text":" The statement of the brother sounds true but is able to lead a man away from the LORD Jesus Christ. He started well but veered off because of the lust for the things of the world. Yes, we do need the things the world provides, but the principles behind them, if allowed to capture our hearts, have the power to steal our hearts from God. The belief that we need these things side by side with our need for God has made many to believe Jesus Christ with their lips, but their hearts are far from Him. They pay lip service to: \""},{"type":"text","text":"But seek (aim at and strive after) first of all His kingdom and His righteousness (His way of doing and being right), and then all these things taken together will be given you besides\"","marks":[{"type":"italic"}]},{"type":"text","text":"(Matthew 6:33, AMPC). "},{"type":"hardBreak"},{"type":"text","text":" The need for the necessities that will make life easier has made many to love the things of the world more than they love God. This is an age-old problem and a dangerous one: to think one can eat from the table of God and balance it with the table of the world: "},{"type":"text","text":"\"Or do we want to make the Lord jealous? Do we think that we are stronger than He\"","marks":[{"type":"italic"}]},{"type":"text","text":"(1Corinthians 10:22, GNT)? The Bible tells us: "},{"type":"text","text":"\"You used to live in sin, just like the rest of the world, obeying the devil—the commander of the powers in the unseen world. He is the spirit at work in the hearts of those who refuse to obey God\"","marks":[{"type":"italic"}]},{"type":"text","text":" (Ephesians 2:2, NLT). If we have renounced the world, its systems, and its way of doing things, we no longer live under the influence of the Presence of the devil but now live in the PRESENCE OF GOD."},{"type":"hardBreak"},{"type":"text","text":" Sadly, many within the Body still struggle with this. No wonder the Psalmist asked: "},{"type":"text","text":"\"How can a young man keep his way pure...\"","marks":[{"type":"italic"}]},{"type":"text","text":" (Psalm 119: 9a)? This question is important, and how we answer determines whose Presence we live in and whose Table we feed from. And we were told: "},{"type":"text","text":"\"By keeping Your word, I have sought You with all my heart; don't let me wander from Your commands. I have treasured Your word in my heart so that I may not sin against You\"","marks":[{"type":"italic"}]},{"type":"text","text":" (Psalm 119: 9b-11). Jesus went further to show us how important God's word is to our living. He told the devil: "},{"type":"text","text":"\"...It is written, Man shall not live and be sustained by (on) bread alone but by every word and expression of God\"","marks":[{"type":"italic"}]},{"type":"text","text":" (Luke 4:4, AMPC)."}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"The things of the world and from the table of the world may look good, but they cannot sustain man. In fact, they are designed to dull the senses of man and lead him completely away from God (Daniel 1). Beloved, when God created the trees and all vegetation, He spoke to the ground to bring forth vegetation and fruit-bearing trees. When He was going to create the living creatures and fishes in the seas, He spoke to the waters to bring forth the living creatures. When He was going to create man, He spoke to Himself. This is why when you remove the vegetation and all trees from the land, they die. If you remove the fishes and all sea creatures from their habitat, they die. Humans know this! Why then is it difficult for man to understand that without God he cannot live?"}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"We see this play out with Moses in the wilderness. When the LORD told Moses that His Presence would no longer go with the children of Israel because of their sin, Moses knew that was like taking a fish out of its habitat. It becomes fair game to every predator. Moses pleaded with the LORD not to send them on the journey without His Presence. He understood the power in living and operating in the Presence of God. The Presence of God is the natural habitat of man. In Him we have everything: "},{"type":"text","text":"\"for in Him we live and move and have our being, as also some of your own poets have said, ‘For we are also His offspring’ ”","marks":[{"type":"italic"}]},{"type":"text","text":" (Acts 17:28). In Him is the foundation of everything. In fact, in His Presence all things consist. Hence the saying that He that has the LORD Jesus Christ has everything."}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"You may seek His blessing, provision, mercy, grace, etc. It is the Presence of God that makes everything worthwhile.
